newsitem.title: UK: BAA says not appropriate windfall tax target.
newsitem.headline: BAA says not appropriate windfall tax target.

text.p: British airports operator BAA Plc said on Thursday it did not expect to be included in the list of companies which would face a utility windfall tax under a Labour government.
A BAA spokesman questioned the basis of a Financial Times report which estimated that the group could face an extra tax bill of more than 500 million stg under Labour's plans.
Shares in BAA were down 15.5 pence at 492.5 at 0914 GMT.
"We don't see ourselves as a utility, in that we don't offer the provision of essential services like electricity and water," a spokesman said.

The Financial Tines based its estimates on suggestions that Labour would calculate a windfall tax on the total return to shareholders by privatised companies. The FT said those businesses which have produced very high returns, such as BAA, would pay proportionately more.

But the spokesman said BAA would reject suggestions that the returns it has provided are "a windfall to shareholders," adding that "nobody knew when we were privatized that retail would become such a strong part of the business, and this is now 50 percent of revenues."
would increase as a result of its planned 4.5 billion stg spending programme which includes the construction of a fifth terminal at Heathrow airport.

"We have a good relationship with Labour. They appreciate that we have fully produced all the capital spending and assets we said we would and recognize our contribution to UK Plc," the spokesman added.
